title: The Silent River
text:
The poet walks along a quiet river early in the morning. Her words describe the water as a silver ribbon that moves slowly between the trees. She writes that the birds sing only when the sun begins to rise.

In the final stanza, the poet compares her memories to the river. Like the water, she says, the past never stops moving, even when it seems still. This comparison suggests that memories remain alive and continue to change the way we see the present.

questions.text: How does the poet describe the water in the first paragraph?
What does the poet compare her memories to?
What can be inferred about the poet's feelings toward the early morning?
options: She finds the early morning calm and peaceful
She is afraid of the river
She wants to leave the village
She dislikes the sound of birds

questions.text: What is the main idea of the second paragraph?
options: Memories continue to influence the present
Rivers should be protected from pollution
The poet has forgotten her past
Music is more important than nature

paragraph_translations: El poeta camina por un río tranquilo temprano por la mañana. Sus palabras describen el agua como una cinta plateada que se mueve lentamente entre los árboles. Ella escribe que los pájaros cantan solo cuando el sol empieza a salir.

En la última estrofa, el poeta compara sus recuerdos con el río. Como el agua, dice, el pasado nunca deja de moverse, aunque parezca quieto. Esta comparación sugiere que los recuerdos siguen vivos y continúan cambiando la forma en que vemos el presente.
